title: Holidays Around the World
text:
In Mexico, families celebrate the Day of the Dead. They make colorful altars for people they love. The altars have flowers, candles and food.

In Spain, people eat twelve grapes at midnight on New Year's Eve. They eat one grape with each bell. This tradition brings good luck for the new year.

questions.text: What do families make in Mexico?
When do people in Spain eat grapes?
options: At midnight on New Year's Eve

questions.text: How do the families feel about the people they remember?
What can we guess about the grape tradition in Spain?
options: It is a happy way to start the new year
It takes place in the summer

vocabulary.definition: tables or places decorated to honor people or things
objects made of wax that give light when lit
small round fruits that grow in bunches
a custom that people follow for a long time

paragraph_translations: En México, las familias celebran el Día de los Muertos. Hacen altares coloridos para las personas que aman. Los altares tienen flores, velas y comida.
En España, la gente come doce uvas a medianoche en Nochevieja. Comen una uva con cada campanada. Esta tradición trae buena suerte para el año nuevo.
